title: The major scale's pattern
summary: The most familiar scale in music, and the pattern of steps that builds it.

steps.title: Major scale
steps.body:
The white keys from C to C make the most common scale in music, the **major scale**. Its sound is the familiar do re mi fa so la ti do.

**Why it matters:** Most pop, film and folk tunes use the major scale. Its sound is so familiar that you recognise it at once.

steps.title: Whole, whole, half
steps.body:
Look at the steps between its notes: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. Written short, that is **W W H W W W H**, where W is a whole step and H a half step. This pattern is the major scale's **scale formula**.

**Why it matters:** The formula works from any starting note. Learn it once and you can build a major scale on any of the twelve keys, white or black.

steps.title: Where the half steps fall
steps.body: In C major the two half steps are E to F and B to C, the two places with no black key in between.

items.prompt: Play C D E F G A B C going up, and say the steps as you go: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
Play E4, then go up a half step: the first H in the formula.
Play B4, then go up a half step: the second H.

steps.title: Do re mi
steps.body: Play the major scale from C and sing do re mi fa so la ti do along with it. Then sing it without playing and check yourself.
